name: Preteritum
subtitle: Past tense: groups I–IV and PocKeTS + X

ruleCards.title: When? Past time markers
ruleCards.rule: Use the past tense (preteritum) for something that happened at a finished time in the past. These words tell you the time is over.
ruleCards.watch: If the sentence starts with the time word, the verb still comes second: Igår jobbade jag hemma.

ruleCards.title: Group I: -ar → -ade
ruleCards.rule: Verbs whose present tense ends in -ar add -de to the present stem: -ar becomes -ade.
ruleCards.watch: This is the biggest group. Most new verbs go here.

ruleCards.title: Group II: -er → +de
ruleCards.rule: Verbs whose present tense ends in -er drop the -er and add -de.
ruleCards.watch: Hör has no -er in the present, but it is still Group II: hörde.

ruleCards.title: Group II: PocKeTS + X → +te
ruleCards.rule: If the stem ends in p, k, t, s or x (PocKeTS + X), Group II verbs add -te instead of -de.
ruleCards.watch: Never köpade or läsde: p and s give -te.

ruleCards.title: Group III: short verbs → +dde
ruleCards.rule: Short verbs that end in a vowel add -dde.
examples: För fem år sedan bodde vi i Tammerfors.
Five years ago we lived in Tampere.

ruleCards.title: Group IV: irregular verbs (1)
ruleCards.rule: Irregular verbs often change their vowel and get no ending. Learn them by heart.
ruleCards.watch: Gjorde is spelled with gj, but the g is silent.

ruleCards.title: Group IV: irregular verbs (2)
ruleCards.rule: More of the most common irregular verbs.
ruleCards.watch: Sa is also written sade, but it is pronounced sa.
